The polar curve $r=12$ and the ray $\theta =\frac{7\pi }{6}$ intersect at the point $P,$ as shown above. What are the Cartesian coordinates of $P?$
worked_solution:
The polar coordinates of $P$ are $(r,\theta )=(12,\frac{7\pi }{6}).$ We can convert the polar coordinates of $P$ to Cartesian coordinates, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =12\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{6}) \\  & =12\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =-6\sqrt{3} \\ y & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =12\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{6}) \\  & =12\cdot (-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =-6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian coordinates of $P$ are $(-6\sqrt{3},-6).$
